items.stem: Why is capturing tasks in an external system better than keeping them in memory?

options.text: It frees mental capacity and reduces the risk of forgetting commitments
options.rationale: Correct: offloading open loops reduces mental load and missed tasks.
Capture organises work; it does not complete it.

options.text: It removes the need to ever prioritise
options.rationale: Prioritisation is still needed after capture.

options.text: It makes every task equally urgent
options.rationale: Capture does not change urgency; prioritisation does.

items.explanation: Correct: an external system offloads memory and lowers the chance of dropped commitments.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: In an urgent/important matrix, which TWO quadrants most deserve proactive scheduling? (Select TWO)

options.text: Important and not urgent (plan and schedule)
options.rationale: Correct: important-but-not-urgent work needs deliberate scheduling or it is crowded out.
Correct: important-and-urgent work must be handled promptly.

options.text: Not important and urgent (minimise or delegate)
options.rationale: These are candidates to delegate or reduce, not to proactively schedule.
These should be eliminated, not scheduled.

items.explanation: Correct: the two important quadrants deserve scheduling; the rest are reduced, delegated or eliminated.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What does research on multitasking suggest about switching between demanding tasks?

options.text: Switching carries a cognitive cost that lowers overall effectiveness
options.rationale: Correct: task switching incurs a cost and reduces effective output on demanding work.
Multitasking does not double output; it usually reduces it.
There is a measurable switching cost.

options.text: It improves accuracy on complex tasks
options.rationale: Switching tends to reduce accuracy on complex tasks.

items.explanation: Correct: switching between demanding tasks has a cognitive cost that lowers effectiveness.
